buildings.purpose: Blocks a monster until the wall breaks, so the bite never reaches the keep.
Shoots the nearest monster and spends wood and gold to cover a side the heroes are not on.
Bursts for a large hit when a monster steps on it, then it is gone.
Feeds the stockpile with food and a little gold during the day.
Raises every attack's damage while the building stands.
Raises mage damage and shortens mage cooldowns while the spire stands.

edges.via: Any living hero who stands on a tree chops wood.
Placing a wall pays its wood cost.
A tower costs wood and gold.
A trap costs wood.
A field costs wood. A farmer pays less.
The forge costs wood and gold.
The spire costs wood and gold.
A barricade pays wood and lays three walls.
A tower costs gold as well as wood.
The forge costs gold as well as wood.
The spire costs gold as well as wood.
Sow places a field without paying wood.
Fields yield food during the build, and a living farmer doubles that yield.
Fields also add a little gold during the build.
Harvest collects food from nearby fields.
Feeding beside the keep spends food and restores keep health.
Feast spends food and heals every living hero.
A kill pays the monster's bounty. A warrior kill pays one extra gold.
Clearing a wave pays the gold the next keep raise costs.
An engineer pays less wood for walls, towers, and traps, and can raise a line of walls.
The engineer's swing repairs the nearest building.
A monster that cannot walk through a wall bites the wall instead of the keep.
A standing tower fires arrows at a monster in range.
A trap damages the monster that steps on it.
Strike, dash, and nova damage monsters in front of the warrior.
Guard cuts the damage of bites against that hero.
Bolt, fireball, and meteor damage monsters. Frost slows them.
Mark makes a monster take more damage. Volley and the shot damage it.
A living scout reveals the next wave's directions before the last five seconds.
A living scout reveals one extra chunk ring on the shared map.
The map table at (0, 160) shows explored chunks to a hero within 80.
A standing forge multiplies attack damage for every hero.
A standing spire raises mage damage and shortens mage cooldowns.
A monster in reach of the keep bites it. A boss slam hits harder.
A monster that is closer to a hero than to the keep bites the hero.
A goblin is the wave-1 biter. It is slower and softer on the first night.
A skeleton is a tougher biter than a goblin.
A wolf is the fast biter from the concept sheet.
The troll is the concept ogre: a large slow biter.
A bat is the small winged biter. It still pays a bounty when it dies.
The boss is the dark rider. Its slam hits the keep harder.
Killing a boss adds one relic the party does not already hold.
Heartwood raises the keep's maximum health.
Whetstone adds damage and swiftness adds move speed.
Granary adds extra food to the field yield.
Killing a fast, armored, or enraged elite adds one relic the party does not already hold.
The spire unlocks the mage meteor. Without it the meteor does not cast.
Raising the keep spends wood and gold. That payment stakes the next ring of houses, and the wall is what makes the ring a city.
Each full ring of standing houses mints one gold on the town-tax beat. Towers, the forge, and the spire spend that gold.
Sow, harvest, or working the day banks labor. Each labor point stakes one croft, which is a field, and pays one wood.
Overlapping monsters push apart so two bodies cannot share one spot.
Monster bodies block each other, so a gap in a wall lets one through at a time.
A hero stops on a monster. The warrior dash is the one pass through a monster.
A living hero stops on another living hero.
The keep is solid. A hero stops at the wall.
The keep is solid. A monster bites it from the edge.
Raising the keep spends wood and gold inside radius 100. There is no card pick.
Each keep rank widens the build radius and pulls the camera back.
The outer ring is dead wood: bare trunks, no crown, and no wood. Living trees are the green ones.
A living hero who stands on a chest opens it once and the room gains 24 gold.
Night 1 is two goblins on the bearings of the two nearest living portals. A broken portal's bearing is left out.
A dead portal claims its chunk. A build outside the keep disc and outside that chunk fails with The land is not held. Raising the keep does not claim the map.
A strike on a portal breaks it. The next night does not spawn on that bearing.
A quarry holds 40 stone. An engineer takes 2 per tick and any other living hero takes 1.
The quarry is the engineer's walk. Stone walls are why the engineer leaves the yard.
A field can be sown only on meadow. Pine refuses the sow and spends nothing.
A wall placed while the room can pay 8 stone and 4 wood is a stone wall with 280 health. A wood wall stays at 170.
Any living hero chops a pine that still has wood. The pine forest refills a wall line after the yard trees are cut. A yard tree in reach takes the chop.
Waking a camp spends 8 gold and adds one ally who does not take a seat.
A shrine grants one relic the party does not hold.
A hermit reveals the next chunk ring. A living scout already reveals one extra ring.
The merchant sells food for gold.
The merchant sells stone for gold.
